root_cause.text: The virtio vsock MSG_ZEROCOPY path in virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb() incorrectly used msg->msg_iter.count after virtio_transport_fill_skb() had already consumed the iterator, causing msg_zerocopy_realloc()/mm_account_pinned_pages() to receive 0 on the last skb and bypass RLIMIT_MEMLOCK pinned-page accounting.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb() used iter->count for msg_zerocopy_realloc() “after virtio_transport_fill_skb() has already consumed the iterator via __zerocopy_sg_from_iter(), so on the last skb, iter->count will be 0, skipping the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK enforcement,” and the patch fixes this by passing the original pkt_len explicitly instead of reading iter->count.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an explicit packet-length parameter to virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb() so zero-copy skb initialization can use caller-provided length information.
intent_record.what: The function signature of virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb() was changed to add a new parameter, size_t pkt_len, inserted between the existing struct msghdr *msg and bool zerocopy parameters.
intent_record.how: This extends the function interface so callers can provide the packet length explicitly when initializing a zero-copy skb, enabling later use of that length inside the function or downstream logic instead of relying only on existing arguments.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the actual packet length instead of msg_iter count when reallocating zerocopy metadata in virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb().
intent_record.what: In virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb(), the local variable `struct iov_iter *iter = &msg->msg_iter;` was removed, and the second argument to `msg_zerocopy_realloc()` was changed from `iter->count` to `pkt_len`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, zerocopy buffer allocation/reallocation now uses the packet length passed into the function instead of the current message iterator byte count, avoiding a size decision based on iterator state and making the allocation match the actual packet being prepared.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the packet length into zerocopy skb initialization so MSG_ZEROCOPY uses correct pinned-page accounting after the message iterator has been consumed.
intent_record.what: A comment was expanded to explain that pkt_len must be passed because the message iterator has already been consumed by virtio_transport_fill_skb(), making iter->count unusable for RLIMIT_MEMLOCK pinned-pages accounting in msg_zerocopy_realloc(), and the call to virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb() was updated to add pkt_len as a new argument between info->msg and can_zcopy.
intent_record.how: At runtime, zerocopy skb initialization now receives the original packet length explicitly instead of relying on an already-consumed message iterator state, allowing correct RLIMIT_MEMLOCK pinned-page accounting for MSG_ZEROCOPY sends and preventing incorrect memory lock accounting during zerocopy transmission.
